items.note: It answers the question directly: Pro at $69 churned 83% (10 of 12), against 12.5% (1 of 8) for Pro at $49. Of the $69 cancellations, 7 were in August and 3 in September. I checked these figures against the data and they are correct. It also says the timing is inferred because the file has no price history.
It excludes all 15 is_trial=yes accounts and explains why.
It excludes the 5 @ourco.test QA accounts, leaving 40 real paying accounts.
It counts an account as churned when cancel_month is filled in (15 of 40 overall). The per-plan counts are correct.

The answer isn't written for a CEO. It is a long analyst report with numbered sections, tables, account IDs, raw column names like `is_trial` and `@ourco.test`, and operational to-dos. It also wanders into trial conversion, which wasn't asked.
The limit was 5 bullets. The answer has 5 sections, a table, about 15 bullets and 6 recommendations, far beyond that.
It doesn't suggest any chart or say what to plot.

It says the sample is small (40 paying accounts) and that the percentages should be treated as directional. It also notes that the price-change timing is inferred. This is thin and appears only as the last recommendation. It doesn't say how confident the conclusion is for the 12-vs-8 Pro comparison itself.
